<reason>Side B (PRO) won a close, high-quality debate. B's decisive move was the concession trap: when A answered the archive pressure question with "the holder pays the photocopy, as part of surrender," B correctly identified that locating, digitizing, and translating a century of records is itself funded provenance work by the former power after title passes — i.e., a core plank of the motion, "accepted and renamed." A's counter-drawing a line between "finishing the return" and funding research/conservation/capacity was coherent but thin, since it conceded that restitution is not complete at shipment even on A's own account. B also defused A's strongest attack (paternalism/conditionality) by consistently framing money as post-title, recipient-defined, and answering the shrine/reburial question with "I keep paying, and I call it respect." A landed real counterpunches that B never fully closed: the political-economy argument that no treasury writes an unconditional, unauditable check, so conditions inevitably regrow through finance ministries, and that paying for conservation the community may decline renders the money "general aid rebranded." These keep the margin narrow. Both sides used the Q1/Q2 and A1/A2 formats correctly and answered pressure directly; both were vivid and grounded without fake precision. B's execution cost — clipped opening, rebuttal 2, and closing — slightly reduces visible completeness, but the visible content still built the clearer path to victory on the motion as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's closing crystallization of A's A1 answer: "Copying a century of expedition records... is not postage. It is a funded program of provenance work, paid for by the former power, delivered after title passes. That is the motion. My opponent has not rejected funded restitution; he has accepted it and renamed it." This was the debate's decisive exchange, converting A's own concession into the proposition's core, compounded by "litigation and shame are not mechanisms; they are the status quo wearing a bow" against A's clean-break accountability.</best_rebuttal>
